title: Social Categories in Interaction
description: Drawing on conversation analytic research, this course explores how social categories, including those traditionally of interest to sociologists (e.g., gender, race, sexuality), are used by participants in naturally occurring interactions. Methodological challenges and debates in this area are also examined. Graduate students who register for this cross-listed course will attend the weekly lectures, additional weekly seminar-type meetings with the instructor, and will complete an expanded set of the assignments.

title: The Analysis Of Interaction In Institutional Settings
description: This seminar focuses on how the dynamics of interactional processes contribute to the constitution of formal settings of social action.

title: Theorizing Social Action in Interaction
description: This course takes up ubiquitous matters of social action, especially in co-present interactions, by tracing the lineages of sociological theories of action. It is grounded in close reading of key developments in theorizing and empirically investigating social action in interaction evident in the writings of both classical and contemporary sociologists.

title: Video Study Of Social Interaction
description: This course examines visible aspects of social interaction. It explores theorganization of gesture, gaze, and body movement in the production of interaction through a survey of published research and direct inspection ofrecordings of ordinary social occasions.

title: Sociology Of Law
description: Selected topics in the sociological analysis of legal stuctures and processes, and of theories of jurisprudence.

title: Sociology of Health
description: In this course we review some of the interdisciplinary literature on the relationship between human health and social forces, with a focus on research and theory in the academic field of sociology.

title: Seminar In Language And Social Interaction
description: The seminar will explore selecte topics in the analysis of naturally occurring conversation with an emphasis on conversational exchange as a form of social interaction.

title: Seminar In Socialization
description: Selected topics in social development and social learning theory will be discussed.

title: Seminar on Gender
description: Current research, theories and concepts of gender will be considered. Topics vary from quarter to quarter and by instructor.

title: Seminar on Gender
description: Current research, theories and concepts of gender will be considered. topics vary from quarter to quarter and by instructor.

title: Sociology of Masculinities
description: This is a survey course covering the sociology of masculinities, which is a subfield that primarily engages the sociologies of gender and sexualities. The course covers theoretical frameworks in the field, key debates, and engages with diverse empirical work.

title: Gendered Violence
description: Examines the relationship between the gender system and violence, exploring how the gender system facilitates and constrains various types of violence and how violence shapes understandings of gender.

title: Transgender Studies
description: Examines the history of Transgender Studies as a field of research with a focus on Transgender Studies work within Sociology.

title: Seminar on the Life Course
description: Examines theoretical and methodological approaches to the study of the lifecourse. The dynamic relation between changing social structures, institutions, and life patterns is emphasized.

title: Social Network Analysis
description: Introduction to concepts, methods, and applications of social network analysis.

title: Seminar On Gender, Race, and Class
description: An examination of the intersection of race, class, and gender in empirical and theoretical socialogical work.

title: Seminar on Sexualities
description: Research and theory on sexual meanings, identities, behavior, and communities.

title: Development and its Alternatives
description: The seminar will explore a range of theories issues and case studies in the sociology of development and social change, primarily in the Third World. Topics and cases covered will vary according to students' and instructor's interests.

title: Climate Justice
description: Explores the diverse meanings and impacts of the concept and practice of the term climate justice as used by scholars, governments, social movement organizations, and activists to imagine and create a sustainable, equitable, democratic world for future generations.

title: Earth in Crisis
description: Explores the causes and consequences of climate change on a global scale, covering the state of the science in layman's terms, the current and future social impacts of climate change, the global negotiations process, and climate justice activism.

title: Sociology of Globalization
description: Overview of the sociology of globalization and theories of globalism. Topics include: the politics of globalization, transnational state apparatuses; social movements; global civil society; transnational migrations; globalization and race/ethnicity; gender and globalization; local-global linkages.

title: Global Culture
description: The course addresses cultural dimensions of globalization including migration, diasporas and ethnic 'others', multiculturalism, hybridity, problems of intercultural representation and stereotypes, fundamental problems of global cognition (eurocentrism, orientalism), cosmopolitanism, and transnational aesthetics.

title: Globalization History and Theory
description: The course addresses contemporary debates on globalization focusing on the periodization and time dimension of globalization, globalization and capitalism, globalization and modernity, and the rise of emerging societies.

title: Globalization and Resistance
description: Perspectives on the multiple, unfolding processes of globalization and attendant structural transformation; critical assessment of emergent forms of resistance/emancipation, from the struggles of women, displaced communities, and peoples of color, to the global justice movement and new paths to revolution.

title: Global Political Economy
description: An advanced graduate seminar covering recent theory and research about global production systems, including developments in world-systems theory, flexible production, post-fordism, and global commodity chains.

title: Introduction to Global, International, and Development Sociology
description: Introduces students to the range of core issues and debates within the fields of global, international, and development sociology, from political economy to culture, gender to REN, social movements to micro-issues.

title: New Modernities
description: Contemporary emerging societies don't simply adopt the model of western modernity. Modernities and capitalisms are analytics that seek to address these questions. Course examines social debates and reflexivities in emerging societies as well as the entanglement of modernities.

title: Conflict, Identity, and The Nation
description: The course focuses on three different but correlated themes: 1)The sociological meaning of "the nation" and the conceptualization of national identity; 2) The comparative sociological history of nationalism and identity; 3) The correlation between identity, conflict, and global change.

title: The World in 2050: Sustainable Development and Its Alternatives
description: Explores the diverse meanings and impacts of the concept and practice of the term sustainable development as used by scholars, social movement organizations, communities, and activists to imagine and create a sustainable, equitable, democratic world for future generations by 2050.

title: Women, Culture And Development
description: Identifying, reading, and critiquing theoretical and empirical materials from all regions of the Third World that address the interrelated themes ofwomen, culture, and development.

title: Sociology of Latin America
description: Examines social, political, economic, and cultural trends in Latin America in historical context, including but not limited to political economy, development processes, women, indigenous people, revolutionary movements, transnational migration, and different debates, theories and perspectives for studying Latin America.

title: Race, Crime, and Punishment
description: Critical analysis of theory and research on the racial-ethnic dimensions of crime and punishment. Focal topics include: race and the incidence of crime; racial disparities in the criminal law; mass incarceration and communities of color.
